climate.overview_html: The dominant new development is the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 “The Point of Return,” released 21 October, which officially declares the 1.5°C “no-or-limited-overshoot” pathway lost: global GHG emissions were essentially flat at 58.4 GtCO2e in 2025, current policies point to 2.6–2.8°C, and a lowest-possible-overshoot path requires 18% cuts by 2030, 45% by 2035, and 69% by 2040. The US logged the largest G20 emissions jump (+133 Mt CO2e). With COP31 opening 9 November in Antalya, Australian minister Chris Bowen named 10 co-facilitators across five ministerial pairs (finance, adaptation, mitigation, just transition, oceans) on 21–22 October. The backdrop remains China’s 22 October position paper, the UN Secretary-General’s “dangerously short” warning, and the suspended IPCC AR7 plenary.

items.source: UNEP / DownToEarth / Nature News / NatureWorldNews / GreentechLead
items.headline: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 “The Point of Return”: 1.5°C Overshoot Now Inevitable; Global Emissions Flat at 58.4 GtCO<sub>2</sub>e in 2025; Current Policies Track to 2.6–2.8°C; Lowest-Overshoot Path Needs 18% Cuts by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040; US Leads G20 Emissions Rise
items.summary: UNEP's annual Emissions Gap Report, released October 21 and titled 'The Point of Return', officially declares that the opportunity to limit warming to 1.5°C with 'no or limited' overshoot has been lost. Global GHG emissions were approximately 58.4 GtCO₂e in 2025 — essentially unchanged from a revised 58.5 GtCO₂e in 2024 — as a fall in land-use and wildfire emissions offset continued growth in fossil CO₂. The drop is too small relative to measurement uncertainties to confirm a peak. Existing NDCs, if fully implemented, would cut emissions by only 5–8% by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035; a lowest-possible-overshoot path that peaks warming at 1.7–1.8°C before returning to 1.5°C by century's end requires cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, and 69% by 2040, plus removal of approximately 320 Gt CO₂ from the atmosphere. Under current policies, warming reaches 2.6–2.8°C. Among G20 nations, the US logged the largest emissions increase (+133 Mt CO₂e), driven by rising electricity demand and a coal rebound, partly attributed to the US exit from the Paris Agreement. On the positive side, solar PV capacity has grown seven times faster than projected since Paris and renewable electricity capacity has tripled faster than anticipated.

items.headline: COP31 Names 10 Co-Facilitators to Steer Key Climate Talks in Antalya: Australia’s Bowen Appoints Five Ministerial Pairs Covering Finance, Adaptation, Mitigation, Just Transition and Oceans; Turkey Expects 85 World Leaders, Record 159 Pavilions
items.summary: Australian Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen, presiding over COP31 negotiations, announced on October 21–22 that ten senior representatives — five ministerial pairs — will co-facilitate the key negotiating tracks at Antalya: (1) climate finance and the Baku Finance Goal, (2) adaptation and the Global Goal on Adaptation, (3) mitigation and NDC implementation, (4) just transition, and (5) oceans and coastal ecosystems. Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum said Turkey expects 85 world leaders at the November 11–12 World Leaders' Summit, and that a record 159 pavilions and 90 delegation offices have been approved. Xinhua reported on October 23 that the Turkish co-presidency is framing COP31 as a 'policies implementation' summit, seeking to operationalise the Baku Finance Goal, the Loss and Damage Fund, and Article 6 carbon markets. The summit runs November 9–20 in Antalya.

items.headline: China Sets COP31 Antalya Priorities: Demands Detailed Roadmap for US$300 Billion Annual Climate Finance Goal, Opposes Carbon Border Mechanisms as Trade Barriers, Pledges to Speak for Developing Nations
items.summary: China's Vice Minister of Ecology and Environment Li Gao published Beijing's COP31 positions on October 21–22. Top priorities: (1) compelling developed countries to deliver a concrete implementation roadmap for the US$300 billion annual climate finance goal agreed at COP29; (2) opposing the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and similar unilateral trade measures as violations of UNFCCC common-but-differentiated responsibilities; (3) demanding the global stocktake focus on implementation gaps in developed-nation commitments rather than developing-nation ambitions; (4) tripling adaptation finance. China intends to attend at the highest level. The positions set up a significant clash with the EU and some of the Turkish presidency's electrification targets at Antalya.

items.headline: UN Secretary-General Guterres: World Falling “Dangerously Short” on Climate Action Ahead of COP31; El Niño and Record Heat Amplify Urgency
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres issued a stark statement on October 21 calling the world 'dangerously short' on climate action, referencing record-breaking heat, devastating floods, and an unprecedented El Niño as making accelerated action 'ever more urgent.' A concurrent UN release emphasised that the NCQG agreed at COP29 must be operationalised and that the UNFCCC process faces a credibility crisis with climate-vulnerable nations. With COP31 in Antalya opening November 9 and a World Leaders' Summit set for November 11–12, diplomatic pressure is intensifying.

items.source: The Standard HK / CTV News / Reuters
items.headline: IPCC Plenary Suspended in Addis Ababa Without Agreement on AR7 Timeline: Saudi Arabia, India and China Back 2029 Delay Over 2028 Target; Small-Island and LDC Delegations Walk Out; IPCC Chair Skea Calls for Swift Resolution; AI Use Guidelines Agreed
items.summary: The IPCC's plenary in Addis Ababa was suspended on October 16 without agreement on the AR7 timeline. Saudi Arabia, India and China backed a 2029 completion date; the EU and AOSIS want 2028 to inform the second global stocktake. Delegations from least-developed countries and small island states were forced to leave before a vote could be held as the session overran. IPCC chair Jim Skea called on October 19 for a swift resolution, warning that COP31's loss-and-damage and adaptation tracks may proceed without an agreed scientific baseline. One productive outcome: the plenary reached consensus on guidelines for AI use within IPCC assessments — the first such policy decision for the panel.

items.headline: South Africa at COP31: As Climate Shocks Intensify, Pretoria Pushes for Substantially More Adaptation Finance; Aligns with G77 Demand to Triple Adaptation Funding by 2035
items.summary: South Africa is entering COP31 with adaptation finance as its top priority, arguing that developing nations most vulnerable to climate shocks have been shortchanged in NCQG negotiations dominated by mitigation framing. The piece cites intensifying floods, drought cycles, and coastal erosion in southern Africa as the political driver. South Africa aligns with G77 demands for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, mirroring the European Parliament's October resolution position. While adaptation funding pledges have grown, actual disbursements remain far below commitments — a structural issue South Africa and the African Group plan to press at Antalya.

major_events.name: Typhoon Champi (Rosal) — Taiwan Island-Wide Shutdown 23 Oct; 600+ Flights Cancelled; Weakened to 173 kph Sustained / 198 kph Gusts; Track Models Split — NE Taiwan Brush, Direct Landfall, or Kyushu (Japan) Strike; Zhejiang 36 Ferry Routes Suspended
major_events.status: As of 23 Oct morning local: Taiwan issued an island-wide shutdown — schools, government offices and the stock exchange all closed. Over 600 flights cancelled (262 domestic + 350+ international). The storm weakened overnight: maximum sustained winds approximately 173 kph (gusts 198 kph), down from 184/227 kph on 22 Oct. Track uncertainty remains extreme: AI-based ensemble models keep Champi offshore of Taiwan’s northeastern tip; many physics-based NWP models show a brief northeastern Taiwan landfall; Zoom Earth guidance tracks landfall ~93 km south of Sasebo in Kyushu, Japan. China’s Zhejiang province suspended 36 passenger ferry routes; heavy rain warnings cover coastal Zhejiang and Fujian. Taiwan’s Central Mountain Range expected to weaken the system further as it transits northward.
major_events.impact: Taiwan: island-wide shutdown (schools, government, stock exchange); 600+ flights cancelled; land warning active (Yilan, Hualien, Taitung, Pingtung); heavy to extreme rain east coast spreading north. China: Zhejiang 36 ferry routes suspended; heavy rain warnings coastal Zhejiang & Fujian; Shanghai/Hangzhou/Fuzhou/Wenzhou airports on disruption watch. Japan: Kyushu on possible late-week impact watch per some model guidance. Guam: post-passage damage assessment ongoing.

major_events.name: SE Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — Day 26+ — ASMC Level 3 Alert; ~1.9 Million Hectares Burned; 40 Million People Exposed; Protests Demand National Disaster Declaration
major_events.status: As of 23 Oct: No significant change. Satellite estimates put total 2026 burned area in Indonesia at nearly 1.9 million hectares. Greenpeace estimates ~40 million people across Kalimantan and Sumatra exposed to hazardous air quality for over two months. Protests have erupted in several Indonesian cities demanding a national disaster declaration. Indonesia’s health ministry recorded 283,270 respiratory illness cases across seven provinces (as of 13 Oct; actual figure higher). Super El Niño and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole continue to suppress rainfall. ASEAN pre-summit enforcement review scheduled for November.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 283,270+ respiratory illness cases (7 provinces), 4+ deaths, protests demanding national disaster declaration; Malaysia: schools closed in affected areas; Singapore: legal actions against 7 companies ongoing; Papua New Guinea: smoke reaching Port Moresby; India: Great Nicobar Island affected; ~40 million people exposed for 2+ months across Kalimantan and Sumatra.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Champi dominated the 23 October regional weather picture. Taiwan issued an island-wide shutdown on 23 October — closing schools, government offices and the stock exchange — as Champi, weakened overnight to 173 kph sustained (gusts 198 kph) from its 22 October peak of 184/227 kph, made its closest approach to the northeastern coast. Over 600 flights were cancelled (262 domestic, 350+ international). Track guidance remained sharply split: Zoom Earth’s live tracker showed some guidance targeting Kyushu, Japan; many NWP models showed a northeastern Taiwan landfall; AI ensemble models kept it offshore. China’s Zhejiang suspended 36 ferry routes and issued heavy rain warnings for coastal Zhejiang and Fujian. On the other major event, the SE Asian transboundary haze crisis enters day 26+ with protests erupting in Indonesian cities: satellite data now put 2026 burned area at nearly 1.9 million hectares, and Greenpeace estimates 40 million people across Kalimantan and Sumatra exposed for more than two months.

items.source: Taipei Times / The Nation Thailand / SCMP / Zoom Earth / Malay Mail / Insurance Journal
items.headline: Typhoon Champi 23 Oct: Taiwan Shuts Island-Wide (Schools, Stock Exchange); 600+ Flights Cancelled; Storm Weakens to 173 kph; Track Models Split — NE Taiwan Landfall vs. Offshore Brush vs. Kyushu Strike; Zhejiang Suspends 36 Ferry Routes
items.summary: On October 23, Taiwan's government issued a full-island shutdown — schools, government offices and the stock exchange closed — as Typhoon Champi made its closest approach to the northeast coast. The Nation Thailand reported over 600 flight cancellations (262 domestic, 350+ international). The storm had weakened overnight: maximum sustained winds fell to approximately 173 kph (gusts 198 kph), down from 184/227 kph on October 22. Track guidance split sharply: AI-based ensemble models kept Champi offshore of Taiwan's northeastern tip; many physics-based NWP models showed a brief landfall over northeastern Taiwan; and Zoom Earth's live tracker showed some guidance pointing toward landfall ~93 km south of Sasebo, Kyushu, Japan. China's Zhejiang province suspended 36 passenger ferry routes and issued storm surge and heavy rain warnings; Shanghai, Hangzhou, Fuzhou and Wenzhou airports remained on disruption watch. The storm had earlier peaked at Category 5-equivalent intensity over the Philippine Sea. Taiwan's Central Mountain Range was expected to further weaken the system as it transited northward.

items.source: Greenpeace / Down to Earth / Al Jazeera / France 24 / Malay Mail
items.headline: SE Asian Haze Day 26+: Satellite Data Shows ~1.9 Million Hectares Burned in Indonesia in 2026; Greenpeace: 40 Million People Exposed 2+ Months; Protests Demand National Disaster Declaration; ASMC Level 3 Alert Continues
items.summary: The Southeast Asian transboundary haze crisis continues into its 26th day-plus with no significant improvement. Satellite estimates now put total burned area in Indonesia at nearly 1.9 million hectares in 2026 — substantially above the 637,000 ha figure for January–August alone. Greenpeace estimates approximately 40 million people across Kalimantan and Sumatra have been exposed to hazardous air quality for over two months. Protests have erupted in several Indonesian cities demanding a national disaster declaration. Indonesia's health ministry recorded 283,270 respiratory illness cases across seven provinces (as of October 13; actual figure higher). The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre maintains Alert Level 3. Smoke has reached Papua New Guinea's capital Port Moresby and India's Great Nicobar Island. Super El Niño and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole continue to suppress monsoon rainfall over fire-prone Borneo and Sumatra.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s largest capacity development: Atmos Renewables completed the acquisition of BayWa r.e.’s Australian portfolio on 16 October, taking its total operating-plus-construction capacity beyond 2 GW and adding the ~800 MW Bullawah Wind Farm development in New South Wales. China Huaneng announced the full grid-connection on 21 October of a 960 MW wind-solar-storage hybrid in Inner Mongolia — the first coal-flexible-dispatch plus renewables integration project of its kind in China, pairing 810 MW wind, 150 MW solar and a 60 MW/240 MWh grid-forming battery. EirGrid’s data showing 15% of Ireland’s H1 2026 wind electricity wasted due to grid constraints continues to sharpen the debate around Europe’s transmission investment gap.

items.source: PV Magazine Australia / Baker McKenzie / Enerdata / Power Technology
items.headline: Atmos Renewables Acquires BayWa r.e.’s Australian Renewable Portfolio — Yatpool Solar (106 MW), Hughenden Solar (20 MW), Bullawah Wind Development (~800 MW) — Pushing Total Capacity Beyond 2 GW; BayWa Retreats to Core European Markets
items.summary: Atmos Renewables, the renewable energy arm of Igneo Infrastructure Partners, finalised on October 16 the acquisition of a portfolio of Australian renewable assets from BayWa r.e., announced publicly October 19. The acquired assets include: Yatpool Solar Park (106 MW, Victoria, operating since 2021, offtake with Flow Power); Hughenden Solar Park (20 MW, Queensland, operating since 2018, PPA with CS Energy); the Bullawah Wind Farm development in New South Wales (~800 MW wind plus 359 MW/718 MWh battery per Enerdata, though PV Magazine notes only 262 MW access rights for the first wind stage); and several earlier-stage projects. The deal pushes Atmos's combined operating and in-construction capacity beyond 2 GW. Baker McKenzie advised BayWa; purchase price was not disclosed. BayWa r.e. is retreating from non-core markets amid its parent company's financial restructuring.

items.headline: China Huaneng Fully Grid-Connects 960 MW Wind-Solar-Storage Hybrid in Inner Mongolia: 810 MW Wind + 150 MW Solar + 60 MW/240 MWh Grid-Forming BESS + Coal Flexible Dispatch; First Integrated Coal-Renewables Retrofit of This Scale in China
items.summary: China Huaneng announced on approximately October 21 the full grid connection of a 960 MW wind-solar-storage project at Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia. The facility comprises 810 MW wind, 150 MW solar PV, a 60 MW/240 MWh grid-forming battery energy storage system, and a 20 Mvar static synchronous condenser, all underpinned by a 220 kV step-up substation. The project is paired with a coal-fired power plant operating in flexible dispatch mode — described as the first project of this kind in China, representing a model for transitioning coal capacity alongside new renewables on the same grid connection. Expected annual output: approximately 2.3 billion kWh. Ulanqab is a key hub for ultra-high-voltage transmission lines connecting Inner Mongolia to coastal load centres.

items.headline: AMEA Power Signs Agreements for 250 MW/1,000 MWh Battery Storage Project in Uzbekistan’s Bukhara Region; Central Asia’s Largest Battery Commitment of 2026; Executed at Tashkent Energy Sector Investors’ Council 16 Oct
items.summary: UAE-based AMEA Power signed project agreements on October 16 for a 250 MW / 1,000 MWh battery energy storage system in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region (Gijduvan district), announced publicly October 20. It follows AMEA Power's existing 150 MW / 300 MWh BESS under construction near Tashkent (ground broken May 2026). Combined, AMEA Power's total committed Uzbekistan storage is 400 MW / 1,300 MWh. Uzbekistan has been aggressively contracting battery storage to complement growing wind and solar capacity and stabilise a grid experiencing intermittency pressures. No deal price for the Bukhara project was disclosed.

items.headline: EirGrid Data: 15% of Ireland’s Wind Electricity Wasted H1 2026 Due to Grid Constraints; Enough to Power 667,000 Homes; 13%+ of All Renewables Curtailed in First Nine Months; Grid Investment Lag Worsening
items.summary: New EirGrid figures published by RTÉ on October 21 reveal that more than 13% of available wind and solar electricity in Ireland during the first nine months of 2026 could not be used due to grid constraints. In H1 alone, 15% of wind electricity was dispatched down — enough to power approximately 667,000 Irish homes. The figures represent a worsening from 2025 curtailment rates and are above EirGrid's ECP-2.3 projections. Experts cite a multi-year lag between accelerating renewable capacity additions and major transmission infrastructure investment, with Grid West and the North-South interconnector still years from completion.

items.headline: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II Completes Acquisition of Nivala BESS — Finland’s Largest Battery Energy Storage System — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures; Nordic Grid-Balancing Assets Draw Continued Institutional Capital
items.summary: Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II completed its acquisition of 100% of Nivala BESS — Finland's largest battery energy storage system — from Fotowatio Renewable Ventures (FRV), the renewables subsidiary of Abdul Latif Jameel. No deal price was disclosed. Nivala provides frequency and voltage grid balancing services in Finland's electricity market, where curtailment pressure from growing intermittent renewable capacity is rising. The acquisition continues a trend of institutional infrastructure funds acquiring operational Nordic BESS assets as ancillary services revenue models mature.

items.headline: XCF Global Completes All-Stock Three-Way Merger Combining Renewable Fuel Production, Biomass-to-Fuels Development (Southern Energy Renewables) and Carbon-Asset Monetisation (DevvStream); Creates Integrated Renewable Fuels Platform
items.summary: US-based XCF Global completed an all-stock three-way business combination on October 19, uniting XCF's existing renewable fuel production and refining operations, Southern Energy Renewables' biomass-to-fuels development pipeline, and DevvStream's environmental asset management and carbon credit monetisation platform. The merged entity targets the full lifecycle of biomass-based renewable fuel projects from production through carbon credit generation and sale. No financial terms or combined capacity figures were disclosed.

science.overview_html: The week’s science highlights span from ML benchmarking on the hardest targets to foundational perspective-setting. Timed to the active Typhoon Champi, arXiv:2610.22077 (15 October) benchmarks probabilistic AI weather models specifically on tropical cyclones, finding that leading AI models beat ECMWF IFS-ENS at cyclone tracking, but that intensity forecasting and ensemble spread remain weak — the exact failure modes characterising Champi’s uncertain close approach. Tom Beucler and 12 co-authors’ perspective arXiv:2610.09770 (7 October) traces how autoregressive reanalysis-trained models progressed from nowcasting to subseasonal scales in under two years, mapping open challenges at each lead time. The subseasonal reference paper remains Mouatadid et al. in Nature (14 October): probabilistic bias correction doubles AI subseasonal skill at 2–6 weeks and leads the SubX competition. At the science-policy intersection, the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 (21 October) is the most significant climate-science output of the week, while the IPCC Addis Ababa plenary remains suspended on AR7 timeline.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22077 — Can AI Forecast the Extremes? Evaluating Probabilistic Weather Models on Tropical Cyclones: AI Beats ECMWF IFS-ENS on Track; Intensity and Ensemble Spread Remain Weak Points
items.summary: Submitted October 15, 2026, this paper benchmarks several leading probabilistic AI weather models specifically on tropical cyclone forecasting — a high-stakes application where existing evaluations typically use aggregate global skill scores that can mask performance on extremes. Key findings: leading AI models outperform ECMWF IFS-ENS at tropical cyclone track forecasting across multiple lead times. However, intensity forecasting and ensemble spread calibration remain weak compared to the dynamical baseline — models underweight rare, high-intensity values. The paper argues that training objectives favouring large-scale atmospheric state skill systematically compress probability mass away from extreme intensities, and proposes evaluation frameworks better suited to extremes. Particularly relevant alongside the active Typhoon Champi: the failure modes identified here — track vs. intensity and spread — match the forecast uncertainty characterising Champi's close approach on October 23, where AI ensemble guidance diverged sharply from NWP track guidance.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.26145 — Hourly Precipitation Downscaling from km-Scale Regional Climate Simulations (Addison, Kendon, Watson); Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.meta: Addison, Kendon, Watson · arXiv:2610.26145 [physics.ao-ph] · 20 Oct 2026 · NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning
items.summary: Henry Addison, Elizabeth Kendon and Peter Watson present a deep-learning approach to downscaling hourly precipitation from kilometre-scale regional climate model (RCM) simulations to sub-kilometre scales relevant to impact applications (urban flooding, hydrology, agriculture). Accepted to the Workshop on Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning at NeurIPS 2026 (Sydney, December 2026). The work addresses a key bottleneck: as convection-permitting km-scale RCMs become feasible for multi-decade climate runs, translating their output to the finest spatial scales needed for adaptation planning remains computationally prohibitive without statistical downscaling. Connects to the broader question of whether ML downscaling can substitute for dynamical downscaling at the sub-kilometre scale.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.09770 — “Artificial Intelligence Pathways from Weather to Climate” — Beucler et al. (13 authors): How Autoregressive Reanalysis-Trained Models Progressed from Nowcasting to Subseasonal in Two Years; Maps Open Challenges at Each Lead Time
items.meta: Beucler et al. (13 authors) · arXiv:2610.09770 [physics.ao-ph] · 7 Oct 2026
items.summary: Tom Beucler and 12 co-authors published this perspective tracing how autoregressive AI models trained on reanalyses have advanced along the full weather-to-climate prediction pathway. The paper argues that models which now compete with dynamical NWP at medium-range have done so by exploiting temporal self-consistency in ERA5-style reanalyses rather than through physically motivated inductive biases. It maps open challenges: (1) nowcasting — where physics-based data assimilation may retain an edge for convective initiation; (2) medium-range — where AI models are broadly competitive with ECMWF; (3) subseasonal-to-seasonal — where probabilistic bias correction and ensemble post-processing have substantially closed the gap; (4) climate projection — the hardest remaining challenge, where the distributional shift from historical to future states is not captured by reanalysis training. The authors call for hybrid approaches that inject physical constraints at each temporal scale.

items.headline: Mouatadid et al. in Nature: Probabilistic Bias Correction Doubles AI Subseasonal Forecast Skill at 2–6 Weeks; Improves ECMWF IFS for 92% of Temperature and 98% of Precipitation Targets; Leads SubX International Competition
items.summary: Published in Nature on October 14, this paper introduces probabilistic bias correction (PBC) as a post-processing method for AI subseasonal forecasts in the 2–6-week range. Key findings: PBC doubles AI subseasonal forecast skill relative to the uncorrected AI baseline at 2–6-week lead times; it improves ECMWF's dynamical IFS for 92% of temperature prediction targets and 98% of precipitation targets globally; and leads the SubX international subseasonal forecast competition. PBC works by learning to correct systematic errors in the predictive distribution from historical forecast–observation pairs, rather than correcting point estimates. This implies that existing AI weather models have substantial latent skill at subseasonal timescales masked by poorly calibrated probability distributions — a significant finding for operational S2S forecasting and renewable energy planning applications.

items.headline: IPCC Reaches Consensus on Artificial Intelligence Guidelines for Climate Assessment at Addis Ababa Plenary; First Major IPCC Policy Decision on AI Use in Scientific Reports Amid Wider AR7 Timeline Deadlock
items.summary: Amid the broader failure to agree on the AR7 timeline, IPCC chair Jim Skea confirmed on October 19 that the Addis Ababa plenary reached agreement on guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence within IPCC scientific assessments. This marks the first time the IPCC has established formal policy on how AI-generated analysis, AI-assisted literature synthesis, or ML-based projections may be incorporated into its reports — a significant governance step given the rapid growth of ML in climate and atmospheric science. The guidelines address concerns about AI reliability, reproducibility, and uncertainty quantification in scientific assessment contexts. Details were not publicly released. The broader AR7 timeline dispute remains unresolved.

items.title: CarbonFarm Raises €7 Million (Oversubscribed) Series A to Scale AI-Powered Methane MRV for Rice Farming; Led by Colam Impact with Proparco, Suma Capital, Bpifrance; 19 Countries, Expanding to Latin America
items.body_html: CarbonFarm, a Paris-based digital MRV startup, closed an oversubscribed €7 million Series A on 13 October 2026, led by Colam Impact with participation from Proparco, Suma Capital, elea, Working Capital Fund, Albo, Bpifrance and existing investors Serena and Racine². CarbonFarm uses AI satellite imagery, field-data tools and GHG modelling to quantify methane emissions from rice cultivation at field level; rice contributes an estimated 9–12% of global human-caused methane. Improved water management can reduce rice emissions by up to 50% without yield loss. The company operates across 19 countries and is expanding into Latin America.
